what: Sprouts Farmers Market runs about 450 grocery stores in the US that focus on fresh produce, organic and natural foods, and health-oriented products.
customers: Health-conscious shoppers looking for fresh, organic and specialty foods.
money: Fresh produce, meat, seafood and deli.
Packaged natural and organic foods, supplements and household goods.
moat: A clear identity in natural and organic foods, smaller stores that cost less to build, and a large range of private-label products.
risks: Grocery is low-margin and competitive; larger chains expanding organic ranges threaten its niche.
Same-store sales growth has slowed from its 2024–2025 pace.
Analysts rate it a hold despite strong earnings, a sign of doubts about the growth rate.
Food inflation and labour costs pressure margins.
opportunities: Revenue grew from $6.1B in 2021 to $8.8B in 2025, and $9.1B over the last twelve months.
Net income more than doubled from $244M to $524M over the same period.
At about 9 times trailing earnings, the shares price in a sharp slowdown.
Shares fell from 116M to 99M through buybacks.
watch: Same-store sales growth, which shows whether the brand still draws shoppers.
view: Sprouts is a high-quality grocer whose shares now price in a sharp slowdown. Net income more than doubled from 2021 to 2025, margins rose and buybacks reduced the share count, yet the stock trades at about 9 times trailing earnings.

The market’s worry is that the boom in sales growth is over and margins have peaked. Same-store sales have slowed, and larger rivals are expanding natural and organic ranges. That risk is real, but 9 times earnings implies falling profits, not just slower growth.
This turns on same-store sales. If they stay positive and new stores keep opening, the shares look cheap. I think the market is too pessimistic and would see this as a reasonable entry point.
bull: Same-store sales stabilise and the market re-rates an undervalued grower.
bear: Competition and slowing growth squeeze margins and earnings fall.
